item.text: {"text":"FISM scores a candidate using a length-normalized, order-independent sum of historical item embeddings dotted with its target embedding, plus biases; history and target embeddings are separate. FPMC instead adds a user–candidate preference score to a factorized transition score from the previous item, or averaged over the previous basket. FOSSIL replaces FPMC’s user vector with FISM-style history pooling and adds recent-item transitions with global plus user-specific lag weights, sharing item factors across long- and short-term components. Thus, adding historical similarity to sequential scores has substantial precedent; FOSSIL’s lag weights need not follow monotonic recency decay. [FISM](https://chbrown.github.io/kdd-2013-usb/kdd/p659.pdf), [FPMC](https://www.ra.ethz.ch/cdstore/www2010/www/p811.pdf), [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152).\n\nSuggested controls for a SASRec residual, s(i)=s_SASRec(i)+g⟨Σ_t w_t e(x_t),e(i)⟩, with shared embeddings and learned scalar g: compare g=0, normalized uniform weights, normalized recency weights, and last-item-only pooling, keeping history windows and score scaling matched. Shuffle only the residual branch’s history positions while preserving SASRec’s input: degradation tests whether the residual exploits order rather than item membership. Compare popularity-only ranking and SASRec plus a gated log training-frequency score; replace residual dot products with cosine similarity to probe embedding-norm effects. Initially freeze the same SASRec checkpoint and fit only gates, cheaply isolating score-combination benefits; then retrain promising variants under matched budgets. These are proposed ablations, not established results. Select by four-category macro validation HR@10 and inspect per-category gains; recency-specific potential remains unproven until recency beats uniform pooling, last-item similarity, and popularity controls."}
